pages.title: Piers
pages.content:
Six piers, twenty-four minutes

Eastmole (minute 0) is the commuter terminal, with a ticket window. Shipyard Steps (5) serves the workshops and the technical college. Lantern Point (9) is housing and the old light. Customs Stairs (14) is the city centre and the Harbour Office, with the other ticket window. Fishmarket Quay (19) is the market, open from 06:00. Ropewalk (24) is parks and offices.

Tickets are sold at the windows at Customs Stairs and Eastmole, and on board at the other four piers. Every pier has a step-free ramp.

pages.title: Timetable
pages.content:
A sailing day

The first boat leaves Eastmole at 05:40, then every 20 minutes. Morning peak, 07:00 to 10:00, every 15 minutes. Midday, 10:00 to 16:00, every 20. Evening peak, 16:00 to 19:00, every 15, then every 20. The last boat leaves Ropewalk at 23:10 and arrives at Eastmole at 23:34.

Sailings can change when weather stops the service. Notices go up at each pier and on the Notices page.

pages.title: Fares
pages.content:
Paper ticket, or a pass

Single $3.20, any distance on the line. Child single $1.60, ages 5–15; under 5 travel free. Day pass $8.50, until the last boat. Ten-ride book $27.00, paper tickets, no expiry. Monthly pass $74.00, calendar month, named. Bicycle $1.00, added to any ticket.

pages.title: The Boats
pages.content:
Five boats

Morning Tern, Petrel, Kittiwake and Sandpiper are in service. Slack Water is the relief boat. Each boat carries 180 passengers and 24 bicycles and has a step-free ramp. Morning Tern and Petrel were built in 2011, Kittiwake and Sandpiper in 2014, Slack Water in 1998.

pages.title: Crew
pages.content:
Four to a sailing

Every sailing leaves with four crew: a master, an engineer and two deckhands. They come aboard at 05:15 for checks, the ramp test and the engine warm, before the first boat leaves Eastmole at 05:40.

Ruth Adeyemi, master of Morning Tern. Tomas Lindgren, chief engineer. Priya Nair, deck lead. Mateus Carvalho, deckhand on Petrel. Yuna Seo, pier supervisor at Customs Stairs. Ewa Nowak, timetable planner. Samir Haddad, general manager.

pages.title: On Board
pages.content:
Step-free at every pier

Every pier has a step-free ramp, and each boat can take 24 bicycles. A bicycle is $1.00 added to any ticket. Children under 5 travel free. Lost property is kept at the Harbour Office, 1 Customs Stairs.

pages.title: About
pages.content:
A commuter line, on the water

Ushio Line began in 1974 in Calder Bay with two boats and four piers. Ropewalk joined the line in 1996 and Eastmole opened in 2008 as the commuter terminal. The line now runs six piers in twenty-four minutes with five boats.

pages.title: Contact
pages.content:
Contact

Ushio Line Harbour Office, 1 Customs Stairs, Calder Bay.

hello@ushioline.example · +1 555 0142. Office Monday to Saturday, 08:00–18:00. Ticket windows at Customs Stairs and Eastmole every day, 05:15–23:30.

posts.title: Winter timetable from 1 December
posts.excerpt: The winter timetable keeps the 05:40 first boat and the 23:10 last boat. Midday sailings run every 20 minutes as before.
posts.content:
Ewa Nowak has written the winter timetable. The first boat still leaves Eastmole at 05:40 and the last leaves Ropewalk at 23:10. Morning and evening peaks stay at every 15 minutes.

Printed copies are at the ticket windows at Customs Stairs and Eastmole.

posts.title: Fishmarket Quay ramp repairs
posts.excerpt: The ramp at Fishmarket Quay is being resurfaced. The pier stays open with a temporary level ramp.
posts.content:
Resurfacing of the Fishmarket Quay ramp takes place over two weeks. The pier stays open, and a temporary step-free ramp is in place.

Leila Rahimi and the other market sellers have been asked to use the east side of the quay while the work is done.

posts.title: Slack Water in maintenance
posts.excerpt: Slack Water, the relief boat, is out for maintenance. The four service boats cover every sailing.
posts.content:
Slack Water, built in 1998, is in the yard for routine maintenance. Morning Tern, Petrel, Kittiwake and Sandpiper cover every sailing.

Tomas Lindgren, chief engineer, expects the boat back in service before the winter timetable begins.

posts.title: New covers for the ten-ride book
posts.excerpt: The ten-ride book has a new cover. The paper tickets inside are unchanged and still have no expiry.
posts.content:
The ten-ride book, $27.00, now has a stiffer cover that fits a coat pocket. The paper tickets inside are the same as before.

Books bought earlier stay valid. There is no expiry on unused tickets.

posts.title: Bicycle racks move to the stern
posts.excerpt: Bicycle racks on all five boats move to the stern deck. Each boat still takes 24 bicycles.
posts.content:
The bicycle racks move to the stern deck on every boat, next to the ramp. Each boat still takes 24 bicycles at $1.00 added to any ticket.

Deckhands will help during the morning peak.

posts.title: Lantern Point Year 5 trip
posts.excerpt: The Lantern Point Year 5 class makes its one Tuesday trip across the bay. Please give them room on the deck.
posts.content:
On Tuesday the Lantern Point Year 5 class makes its trip across the bay on the morning boat. Priya Nair and the deckhands will meet them at the gangway.

Children under 5 travel free and the class travels on a group ticket.
